title: Graceful tool params: polyglot JSON authoring format and repair advisor
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Goal: Define and implement a tolerant JSON authoring format for tool/function parameters (polyglot-json) that improves backwards compatibility with existing SDKs and provides automated repair suggestions in error payloads. The feature should reduce user friction when model outputs attempt to call tools with slightly mis-shaped parameters and provide clear, machine-readable remediation hints for clients and SDKs.

Background: We frequently see tool invocations where field names are close but not exact (eg. 'start_date' vs 'startDate'), stringified numbers, enums with case differences, or payloads missing optional wrapper objects. Current behavior is strict validation and hard errors, which leads to customer confusion and extra retries. There are many existing tickets on tolerant validation and coercion but no unified format or output payload for repair suggestions.

Proposal: 1) Define a polyglot JSON schema syntax extension that allows explicit canonical names plus a small alias list per field, normalization hints (e.g., coerce_string_to_number, trim_whitespace, case_insensitive_enum), and soft/strict scoring for ambiguous matches. 2) Implement a validation pipeline with three modes: strict (current behavior), suggest (reject but emit actionable repairs), and autocorrect (server-applies safe repairs and returns a corrections summary). 3) Standardize an error/repair payload shape that contains: error_code, human_message, field_diagnostics (list of {field, issue, suggested_fix_examples}), and a compact machine_fix vector that SDKs can apply automatically. 4) Add telemetry events for ambiguous matches, autocorrections applied, and repair suggestion acceptance rates to inform future tuning.

Example schema snippet (authoring-friendly form) and invocation examples are included in acceptance criteria below.

Constraints & trade-offs: - Autocorrect must be conservative: only apply deterministic, low-risk fixes (e.g., trimming, numeric coercion when unambiguous). - Avoid excessive heuristics that mask upstream model/agent bugs. - Telemetry must be privacy-safe (no PII collection). - Backwards compatibility: old clients continue to get existing error behavior unless they opt into suggest/autocorrect modes via a request header or SDK flag.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement schema extension and server-side validator behind a feature flag. 2) Expose a request-level param validationMode: {strict, suggest, autocorrect}. 3) Ship SDK helpers that can consume the repair payload and optionally apply suggested fixes and re-invoke. 4) Beta to select customers and internal experiments, gather metrics, iterate, then default to suggest mode for new tool manifests.

Acceptance criteria: - Format spec published in the docs repo with examples. - Server validates and emits repair payloads in suggest mode for a representative suite of 120 synthetic tool calls with >90% helpful-suggestion rate (measured by internal accept/reapply test harness). - Autocorrect mode applies only safe fixes (no more than 3 deterministic rules) and includes a corrections summary in the response. - SDK patch that consumes the machine_fix vector and can re-submit corrected calls with a single API convenience method. - Telemetry surfaces ambiguous-field-rate and autocorrect-accept-rate on Console per-tool.

Implementation tasks (high level): - Schema DSL: author-friendly alias and normalization hints (ENG-EXP-1). - Validator: fuzzy name matcher, coercion rules, and diagnostics emitter (ENG-XX-validate). - Error payload contract and SDK spec (ENG-XX-sdk). - E2E test harness & synthetics for acceptance metrics (ENG-462891). - Console metrics & dashboard wiring (ENG-271999).

Notes: This ticket focuses on the API and runtime behavior; a separate design ticket will cover the console UX for repair explanations and the editorial work for docs and examples.

2026-03-04 - Design review (Marta Chen): Recommended that human_message focus on remediation steps and that machine_fix be minimal (apply-only instructions). Also suggested explicit opt-in semantics for autocorrect.

2026-03-09 - Security (Leo Grant): Confirmed telemetry plan acceptable if PII redaction is enforced at ingestion. Added requirement to strip string values flagged as potential emails/SSNs from telemetry.
